title: Tenant Feature Profiles: Limit the Features of Each Tenant

chapters.title: Tenant Feature Profiles
chapters.subtitle: Limit the features each tenant is offered

steps.text: By default, every tenant is offered the same features. Tenant feature profiles let the Default tenant decide which features a tenant is offered. In this video, we create a profile, assign it to a tenant, and check the result.

chapters.title: Why feature profiles
chapters.subtitle: Not every tenant needs every feature

steps.text: Without a profile, the Features page of every tenant lists the same features, apart from those reserved for the Default tenant. The administrator of a tenant can enable these features, including ones you would rather not offer.
A feature profile is a named list of rules, created on the Default tenant. When you assign a profile to a tenant, its rules decide which features that tenant is offered.
Several tenants can share one profile, and a tenant without a profile is not restricted. Only the Default tenant manages profiles.

chapters.title: How rules work
chapters.subtitle: Exclude, Include and the order of rules

steps.text: Each rule has a Rule, which is Exclude or Include, and an Expression. The Expression is matched against feature IDs, and it can use wildcards, such as an asterisk.

Rules apply in the order listed, and the last rule that matches a feature decides. Here, the Include rule brings the SMTP Email Provider back after the Exclude rule removed every Email provider. A feature that no rule matches stays available.

A feature is also unavailable when a feature it depends on is excluded. Excluding Workflows therefore removes HTTP Workflows Activities, Timer Workflows Activities, and Session Workflows Activities too.

chapters.title: Enable the feature
chapters.subtitle: Tenant Feature Profiles on the Default tenant

steps.text: Feature profiles belong to the Default tenant, so we start there. Under Tools, Features, let's search for Tenant Feature Profiles.
Each row shows the name of a feature and, beside it, the feature ID. The rules of a profile refer to these IDs.
Select Enable. A notice confirms it, and Multi-Tenancy gets a Feature Profiles entry. The Administrator role has the Manage tenant feature profiles permission by default.

chapters.title: Create a feature profile
chapters.subtitle: A name and a list of rules

steps.text: Open Multi-Tenancy, then Feature Profiles. The list is empty, because no profile exists. Select Add Feature Profile to start a new one.
Name is how the profile appears in the list, on the Tenants page, and in the Feature profile field of a tenant. We call it Basic sites.
Rules is an editor for the list of rules. The hint below it shows an example, an Exclude rule for OrchardCore.Flows.
We add three rules. The first excludes the Workflows feature. The second uses an asterisk to exclude every Email provider, and the third includes the SMTP Email Provider again.
Select Save. The profile appears in the list, with Edit and Delete buttons. As the list grows, the Search box finds profiles by name.
To change a profile later, select Edit. The form is the same, with the current rules, and Cancel returns to the list.

chapters.title: Assign a profile to a tenant
chapters.subtitle: Choose it when you edit the tenant

steps.text: The Tenants page lists every tenant, and a separate video covers creating them. Let's select Edit on Bluebird, a tenant without a profile.
The Feature profile field appears when at least one profile exists, and the Create Tenant page offers it too. Select Basic sites, then Save.
Back on the Tenants page, a badge with the profile name marks the row of Bluebird. Maplewood has no profile badge, because no profile applies to it.

chapters.title: Check the result
chapters.subtitle: What the Features page of a tenant offers

steps.text: Let's compare the Features pages. On the Default tenant, a search for OrchardCore.Workflows lists Workflows and the features that depend on it.
Next, the Features button on the Tenants page opens the Features page of Bluebird. The same search finds nothing, so this tenant cannot enable any of them.
Searching for OrchardCore.Email lists Email and SMTP Email Provider, but not Azure Communication Services Email. The wildcard rule excluded it, and the Include rule restored SMTP.
Maplewood has no profile, so its Features page still lists Workflows. A profile only affects the tenants it is assigned to.
A feature profile limits what a tenant is offered. Create it on the Default tenant, assign it to a tenant, and the Features page of that tenant follows its rules. Thanks for watching.
